headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 2 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: After the opening ITT and Manosque's sprint, the peloton of La Vuelta 26 face a first muntain challenge with a summit finish at Font-Romeu. The line is set atop a cat. 2 ascent, coming in quick succession after the first cat. 1 climb of this edition. But the road is flat to begin with. Will it favour long range attackers or GC contenders? The neutral start is set at 13:10, the start proper at 13:21 after a 5.6 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: Gruissan, back on a Grand Tour map
subtext: Gruissan is a La Vuelta stage town for the second time. On the first occasion, in 2017, it was the finish for stage 2, after the Gran Salida in Nîmes. In the finale, the bunch exploded, Yves Lampaert attacked with 1 km to go, and the Belgian eventually took the stage and La Roja. Gruissan also appeared on the map of the Tour de France, in 2024. That time, the race headed to Nîmes, where Jasper Philipsen sprinted to victory. Wout van Aert was 5th on the day and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings. Gruissan is a classic venue of the Tour de l’Aude Féminin, and was also visited by events such as the Tour Méditerranéen. The most recent winner in Gruissan is Marijn van den Berg, in stage 1 of La Route d’Occitanie 2023.

headline: Big turnout for stage 3 in Gruissan
Echelons before the climbs?
subtext: “The first part of the stage is completely flat, where there might be a bit of a breeze, and then the second part climbs gradually from Prades”, La Vuelta’s technical director Kiko Garcia describes. Indeed, the wind is out in Gruissan and many riders at the start hint it could shape the stage. “I think it’s going to be a bit of an exciting start with some wind, and there might be a possibility to split things in the first hundred kms”, Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) sums up. According to Météo-France, the first 100 kilometres will be marked by east‑southeast winds of 25–30 km/h, gusting to 45 km/h, as the riders head south and southwest. That means the wind will initially blow from the side and then shift to a cross‑tailwind.

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 5.6 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: The assaults led by Ethan Hayter and then Wout van Aert didn’t take the overall lea Tadej Pogacar from the overall lead. The UAE Emirates XRG leader is now followed by two Visma-Lease a Bike riders: Wout van Aert (+9’’) and yesterday’s stage winner, Matthew Brennan (+10’’).

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With his victory in the ITT and his place of third yesterday in Manosque, Tadej Pogacar leads the points standings with 42 points. Since he races with La Roja, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) will be wearing the green jersey again. The British rouleur win the intermediate sprint yesterday and now has 37 points. Matthew Brennan follows with the 30 points he took yesterday at the finish.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) dominated the first two categorised climbs of La Vuelta 26 to become the first leader of the KOM standings with 6 points. Also part of the breakaway, Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) took 4 points, while Ethan Hayter and Sinuhe Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) have 1 each.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Matthew Brennan’s first Grand Tour stage win came with a distinctive jersey: the young British sprinter leads the young riders standings with gaps of 2 seconds to Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and 4’’ to Finn Fisher-Black (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe).

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Matthew Brennan (1st), Ben Tulett (11th) and Wout van Aert (22nd) in the first positions, Visma-Lease a Bike had the best collective performance yesterday. They remain second in the team standings, 3 seconds behind UAE Emirates XRG. Netcompany Ineos are now third (+23’’).

headline: Combativity
subtext: In addition to wearing the green jersey, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) has a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: Stage 3 of La Vuelta 26 is ON!
subtext: The 183-man peloton just passed km 0.

headline: First attack
subtext: Six riders try to get away from the peloton.

headline: 30 seconds
subtext: Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) is among the riders on the move.

headline: Hayter is back on the move
subtext: The six early attackers: Olivier Le Gac (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla), Timo Roosen (Pinic PostNL), and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma). At km 5, Milan Vader (Bahrain Victorious) is chasing with a gap of 42''. The peloton trail by 51''.

headline: The break gets away
subtext: At km 8, Vader is 45'' behind the six leaders, and the peloton are 45'' further behind.

headline: UAE Emirates XRG at the front of the peloton
subtext: One of the main question today at the start amongriders was: will Tadej Pogacar target the stage win in Font-Romeu?

headline: Vader is caught by the bunch
subtext: They are now 2'05'' behind the six leaders.

headline: Hayter is the virtual GC leader (again)
subtext: After Tadej Pogacar snatched La Roja away from him for 0.09 second on the opening ITT, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) virtually leads the overall standings again, just like he did on stage 2. Yesterday, he was already part of the breakaway, and bonus seconds consolidated his bid before he had to let the peloton go in the demanding finale. Today, he is the best rider on GC among the early attackers (13th, +29'').

headline: Gap under control?
subtext: Olivier Le Gac (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla), Timo Roosen (Pinic PostNL) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) head to km 25 with a lead of 2'15''.

headline: An update from Uijtdebroeks
subtext: At the start, Cian Uijtdebroeks (Movistar) spoke about his sensations after he crashed yesterday: “That was a tough night, let’s say, but I’m here! The body feels quite OK, just the feet is a little bit of a problem. There’s maybe like a small fissure, we cannot see a lot because there’s fluid around, but let’s see how it is on the bike and what we can do. You know, for sure I wanted to finish yesterday. Also, in the beginning it was super hard after the crash, I had a lot of pain, but then I tried to not think and not feel it, just push to the line and limit the time loss. Today is a new day again, and we will see how it is and how the feet feels. On the top of Font Romeu we will know again where we are.”

headline: The gap increases to 2'40''
subtext: The breakaway riders are at km 37.

headline: The gap decreases
subtext: After reaching a maximum of 2'40'', the gap is back down to 2 minutes.

headline: 45.7 km covered in the first hour
subtext: The attackers are pushing hard to get away. But the peloton are not giving much leeway.

headline: Wentzel: "If I have the legs, why not?"
subtext: Participating in his fist Grand Tour, Mats Wentzel (Kern Pharma) made today's breakaway after describing his sensations at the start: “I think it’s pretty special, also with the start in Monaco, it doesn’t happen a lot. So far I’ve been enjoying it, trying to take in every moment and let’s see what can come now. [The team is looking for a new sponsor but] we don’t race different than the whole year. We try to show ourselves, we try to look for opportunities, to take them, and just give our best. That’s our mentality, always. [Today] as always we have to look for breakaways. I think it may be a bigger fight today with the possibility of crosswinds at the beginning of the stage. But I don’t think the breakaway will make it to the finish as there’s a pretty long climb with some headwind if I’m not wrong. This can favour the bunch. But it also depends on who wants to pull in the bunch. [I want to be] a rider who can bring results. I like the climbs but I prefer a bit more the shorter climbs than today. It may be a bit too long for me but we’ll see; if I have the legs, why not?”

headline: Cort to chase a final La Vuelta stage win?
subtext: Among the six attackers, Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) is the most experienced and the most decorated. The Danish all rounder is participating in his 5th La Vuelta, his 15th and final Grand Tour as he has announced he will retired at the end of the season, at 33 years old. Cort has won stages on all three Grand Tours, but La Vuelta is where he has best displayed his abilities with six stage wins, including three in 2021.

headline: 2'35'' at km 64
subtext: Tadej Pogacar's teammates still control the gap.

headline: UAE Team Emirates XRG leading the peloton
Sivakov: "We don't want to give away the jersey for free"
subtext: Pavel Sivakov spoke this morning about UAE Emirates XRG's approach to defend Tadej Pogacar's La Roja: “We also have to think day by day. Tomorrow is also a hard day. If it’s really hard to control, obviously we’ll have to save the legs, but we don’t want to give away the jersey for free, that’s for sure. For us, it’s also great to have this extra motivation with the red jersey in the team. Anyway, we have the big favourite. But the red jersey is a big feeling. We won’t chase anyone down today or whatever. We also have to see that the rest of the weeks gonna be really tough, especially tomorrow in Andorra. The day after may also be a crosswinds day. There are some really tricky stages, so we have to be smart about it. It’s gonna be hard to control at the start but if we control it well it’s very doable to control for the red jersey.”

headline: Hard pace in the bunch
subtext: The attackers are 95 kilometres from the finish and the gap is down to 1'40''. The bunch is very stretched.

headline: The peloton is chasing the breakaway
UAE Emirates XRG try to split the bunch
subtext: Crosswinds blow from the left as the race enters the final 90 kilometres.

headline: Echelons!
subtext: There are around 60 riders in the first split with 88 km to go. Tudor and Lidl-Trek help UAE Emirates XRG set a strong pace at the front.

headline: Pogacar takes turns at the front of the bunch
subtext: Netcompany Ineos also participate in setting the hard pace.

headline: Stragglers get back to the bunch, including Gall
subtext: The pace appears to drop in the first peloton. Domen Novak (UAE Emirates XRG) sits up to wait for Joao Almeida, who was at his team car when the bunch exploded.

headline: Calm returns in the bunch
subtext: Stragglers return and the attackers' lead is back on the rise: 1'40'' as they enter the final 75 km.

headline: The breakaway are not giving up easily
The UAE train
subtext: Tadej Pogacar and his seven minutes lead the peloton 1'50'' behind the leaders with 68 km to go.

headline: Memories from Font-Romeu
subtext: Font-Romeu makes its debut as a Grand Tour stage finish. La Vuelta passed here in 2001, on stage 11, a day marked by two emblematic figures of the race. In the 8th of his 17 consecutive participations, Iñigo Cuesta went first at the summit early in the stage. José Maria ‘El Chava’ Jimenez eventually flew to his 8th and penultimate La Vuelta stage win. The sequence with the ascents of Mont-Louis and then Font-Romeu was used in the first half of stage 15 of the Tour de France 2021, en route to Andorra la Vella. Sepp Kuss took what remains the USA’s last stage win in the Tour and Tadej Pogacar was leading the overall standings. At over 1,800 metres above sea level, Font-Romeu is home to France’s Centre national d’entraînement en altitude (national high-altitude training centre). It was created in the 1960s for French athletes to prepare for the Olympic Games in Mexico. Among the many champions who have used these infrastructures, France’s Sylvain Chavanel settled in Font-Romeu. Among his many achievements, he led the overall standings of La Vuelta in 2008 (1 day) and 2011 (4 days).

headline: Will Pogacar go for the win?
Rain on the horizon
subtext: The attackers enter the final 60 kilometres with a gap of 1'20''. It's currently raining at Col de Mont-Louis and at the finish in Font-Romeu.

headline: Onley: "The finale was probably harder yesterday"
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) was 9th yesterday in Manosque, andhe's definitely one to watch on today's finale: “I wasn’t planning on sprinting, I was just in a position to stay safe, and then I realised that the finale was actually quite hard. I started to sprint and ended up in a decent position. I’m feeling pretty good. I mean, today is definitely gonna be similar to yesterday probably, more of a sprint between climbers. The finale was probably harder yesterday but overall with the climbs it’s more selective today I guess. I’m in a good place, pretty relaxed. I was expecting to lose time in the first stage, so there was no stress there. I already gained back a little bit of time on some other guys yesterday. That was a nice bonus; I wasn’t expecting that. It’s three weeks long so a lot can change. I’m just going through each day and seeing what happens.”

headline: Alex Kirsch abandons
subtext: He is the second rider out of La Vuelta 26 after Sergio Chumil's crash yesterday.

headline: Into the final 50 kilometres
subtext: Olivier Le Gac (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility), Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla), Timo Roosen (Pinic PostNL) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) are headed for the intermediate sprint with a lead back up to 2 minutes.

headline: The average speed after three hours: 43.3 km/h
subtext: The peloton just passed the intermediate sprint with a gap of 1'40''. Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) was first across the line.

headline: Results of the intermediate sprint (Villefranche-de-Conflent, km 129)
subtext: 1. Hayter, 20 pts 2. Roosen, 17 pts 3. Le Gac, 15 pts 4. Hellemose, 13 pts 5. Wenzel, 10 pts

headline: 40 kilometres to go
subtext: The road already rises although the climb to Col de Mont-Louis begins 35.6 km from the finish line.

headline: First climb of the day
subtext: The ascent to Col de Mont-Louis is also the first cat-1 ascent of La Vuelta 16: 19.4km at 4.8%.

headline: Johannessen: "We need that guy in the red jersey to miss out on the position"
subtext: Sixth yesterday on his birthday, Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) is among the riders willing to shine today in Font-Romey: “[A win] would be the perfect gift for the 27th and one day birthday! It’s a chance today, I think it’s better than yesterday. I think there might be a break, then we would have someone there, and if not, we will for sure try from the peloton… but we need that guy in the red jersey to miss out on the position in the end for it to be a victory! But we’re still gonna try. I think it’s going to be a bit of an exciting start with some wind, and there might be a possibility to split things in the first hundred kms. We have a team with big guys, so it’s something we look forward to, and then the climb for sure will be decisive.”

headline: Gap under a minute
subtext: With 30 kilometres to go (14km to Col de Mont-Louis), the peloton are 58'' behind the six leaders.

headline: Hellemose accelerates
subtext: As the gap drops down to 30 seconds, Asbjorn Hellemose (Jayco AlUla) accelerates with 28 km to go. Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) and Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) follow him.

headline: 10 kilometres to the summit
subtext: UAE Emirates XRG bring the gap down to 30''.

headline: Wenzel ups the ante with 25 km to go
subtext: Only Cort follows the young climber. They are 8.5 km away from the summit. Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates-XRG) pulls the bunch with a gap of 30 seconds.

headline: Wenzel goes solo
subtext: Under the rain, Kern Pharma's young climber distances Magnus Cort with 7;5 km remaning on the Col de Mont-Louis climb. The gap to the bunch increases to 40''.

headline: Cort is caught by the bunch
subtext: Wenzel is the last rider from the breakaway still ahead of the bunch. His lead is up to 48'' with 6.5 km to the summit.

headline: Fortunato in pursuit
subtext: Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) has attacked from the bunch to try and chase Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) before the summit.

headline: Fortunato is with Wenzel
subtext: They are inside the last kilometre of ascent to Col de Mont-Louis. The peloton trail by 25''.

headline: The race is stopped
subtext: Riders take shelter from the hail.

headline: The stage is cancelled
subtext: The weather conditions made it impossible to continue to Font-Romeu.
